title: Strict coefficient interchange for the open total-tensor map
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a Grothendieck site small in the module universe, $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $V\in\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Write $j^*$ for restriction to $(\mathcal C/V,B_V)$, with $B_V=j^*B$, and $j_{B!}\dashv j^*$ for exact module extension by zero and restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Let $A_\bullet=(A_n,q_{m,n})_{m\ge n\ge1}$ be a strict inverse system of commutative $B$-algebra sheaves with unital $B$-algebra maps, including identity and composition laws, and put $A_{n,V}=j^*A_n$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. All tensors are sheafified tensors of module sheaves, and all complexes are possibly unbounded cochain complexes with signed direct-sum total tensor [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For a $B_V$-complex $Q$ and a $B$-complex $F$ put
$$Q_n=Q\otimes_{B_V}A_{n,V},\quad F_n=F\otimes_BA_n,\quad G=\operatorname{Tot}(j_{B!}Q\otimes_BF),\quad G_V=\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes_{B_V}j^*F).$$
Let $\gamma^B:G\xrightarrow\sim j_{B!}G_V$ and the corresponding $\gamma^{A_n}$ be the ordinary slice tensor chain isomorphisms whose inverses are the open-unit transposes; on extension-presheaf generators their forward maps send $[x]_f\otimes y$ to $[x\otimes j^*y]_f$ [lem-sf-ringed-slice-tensor-generators, lem-sf-ringed-open-total-tensor-kflat]. Brackets mean the image of the direct-sum summand indexed by $f:W\to V$, followed by sheafification [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Use the coefficient-linear maps
$$r_{L,n}:(j_{B!}L)\otimes_BA_n\xrightarrow\sim j_{A_n!}(L\otimes_{B_V}A_{n,V}),\qquad [z]_f\otimes a\longmapsto[z\otimes j^*a]_f,$$
for complexes $L$ on $\mathcal C/V$, and the identity-on-summands scalar-restriction identification $\operatorname{Res}_{B\to A_n}j_{A_n!}\cong j_{B!}\operatorname{Res}_{B_V\to A_{n,V}}$ [lem-sf-cbc-slice-tensor-generator-coherence]. These preserve all quotient transitions. Define
$$T_n=\operatorname{Tot}(((j_{B!}Q)\otimes_B A_n)\otimes_{A_n}F_n),\quad S_n=\operatorname{Tot}(Q_n\otimes_{A_{n,V}}j^*F_n),\qquad \gamma_n=\gamma^{A_n}_{Q_n,F_n}\circ\operatorname{Tot}(r_{Q,n}\otimes1).$$

Let $b^X_n:G\otimes_BA_n\xrightarrow\sim T_n$ and $b^V_n:G_V\otimes_{B_V}A_{n,V}\xrightarrow\sim S_n$ be the balanced coefficient chain isomorphisms, with formula $(x\otimes y)\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes1)$ and inverse $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)\mapsto(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$ [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. Then the following is an equality of $A_n$-linear chain maps, simultaneously for all $n$:
$$\gamma_n b^X_n=j_{A_n!}(b^V_n)\,r_{G_V,n}\,(\gamma^B\otimes1).$$
Both sides send $([x]_f\otimes y)\otimes a$ to $[(x\otimes j^*a)\otimes(j^*y\otimes1)]_f$ on homogeneous presheaf generators. The maps and their inverses preserve each bidegree $(p,q)$, intertwine $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes dy$, and commute with every $q_{m,n}$ before localization. After scalar restriction this is an equality of chain maps of strict $B$-module towers; its localization is an equality in their derived category. It is natural in both complexes and in unital maps of coefficient towers. No flatness, boundedness, completeness, or surjectivity hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Obtain the three normalized chain comparisons from lem-sf-open-total-normalized-comparisons. Use lem-sf-open-total-generator-calculus to compute both composites on source generators, and the inverse left composite on the two-scalar target generators.

To detect equality of coefficient-linear chain maps from the source, apply the scalar-extension adjunction degreewise. Precompose with gamma inverse, then apply the extension/restriction adjunction. The coproduct universal property tests all homogeneous insertions; the tensor and sheafification adjunctions reduce these tests to pure tensors. The adjunction units and GammaNormalization inverse formula identify these tests with the original source generators, with scalar 1. The two computed values agree, giving equality of the left and right chain maps.

Take the source strict diagram D from lem-sf-open-total-source-coefficient-family. After scalar restriction, let i_A be the left comparison and define the target transition E(h)=i_A^{-1} D(h) i_B, in left-to-right composition order. Cancellation proves E(identity)=identity, E(hk)=E(h)E(k) and strictness of the left comparison. Equality of the left and right maps gives strictness of the right comparison.

On a target generator with scalar entries a,b, the inverse formula gives source(ab). The source transition sends it to source(h(ab)); multiplicativity gives source(h(a)h(b)). Applying the new left comparison returns the two-scalar target generator with entries h(a),h(b), by the inverse formula and the inverse-hom identity. Thus the transported target transitions are precisely the required coefficient transitions. Complex naturality is supplied by the generator-calculus lemma.

Extensionality of natural transformations and the levelwise equality give equality after precomposition by any coefficient tower. Applying transpose and the actual localization functor to that equality proves the localized equation. This uses no assumption on flatness, boundedness, completeness or surjectivity.
